feature: Generated planet preview on screen 6 / system information
user_request: Show an image of the inspected planet, drawing visual inspiration from other Elite versions.

references.evidence: Oolite system-information screen includes a revolving textured planet, accessible in flight and docked. Oolite calls it F7; preserve this game screen 6 mapping.

Official renderer supports seeded land and sea colour, polar colours, cloud fraction/colour, atmosphere and rotation. Reference the visual approach; implement native Swift without copying source or assets.
Maintainer documentation describes deterministic planet/texture combinations and textures chosen to match system descriptions.

layout.wide: Keep compact fixed-size facts on the left and place a substantial planet preview on the right. Use available screen width, not the existing 680-point text block for the complete layout. Aim for 320-520 logical-point diameter when space allows; fit the body region above the dashboard/footer.
layout.narrow: Stack the globe below the facts; preserve long PLUGH notes and mission clues. Fit the globe into the remaining content rectangle rather than covering text or controls.
layout.typography: Continue GameTypography.scale and GameTypography.row, including full screen. Resizing may enlarge the planet and layout space, never the glyph size.
layout.style: Black background, existing yellow title and rule, white facts, cyan accents. Planet should be shaded and visibly spherical, not just a wireframe circle.

visual_design.default: Recognisable landmasses, oceans, sparse clouds, polar caps where appropriate, a thin atmosphere rim, one directional light and a gradual day/night boundary. Slow rotation helps reveal geography.
visual_design.lave: Original illustrative temperate/agricultural world: blue oceans, green land, white clouds and a thin blue atmosphere. Do not label invented coastlines or climate as historical fact.
visual_design.variation: Vary terrain scale, coastlines, palette, ocean coverage, clouds and polar extent per system. Use existing physical/description data where available. Economy may guide an artistic preset but government is not a physical surface property; keep geopolitical colouring on maps/labels rather than painting entire worlds red or green.
visual_design.unknown_data: Missing surface details are procedural illustration, not new gameplay or authoritative planetary statistics. A small Generated planet view caption is sufficient.
visual_design.determinism: Key appearance by galaxy number, StarSystem.id and all SystemSeed words with a stable documented hash. Do not use Swift Hasher, unseeded random values, or the simulation RNG. Returning to the planet preserves geography; animation changes orientation only.

integration.screen: Display.presentation dispatches .system into compactScreen in Sources/EliteCore/CompactScreens.swift. Extend this path; account for the legacy system renderer in Sources/EliteCore/Display.swift if still used by exports/tests.
integration.selection: Use game.inspectedSystem and game.inspectedGalaxy, matching the displayed data. Do not use currentSystem or targetSystem when browsing another galaxy. Handle all 8 galaxies and PLUGH.
integration.rendering: Implement in the game renderer using reusable native geometry or a cached procedurally generated texture. Do not ship a single static planet picture for all systems or require online image generation at runtime. Honour existing Frame/world graphics conventions.
integration.ownership: Pure Sendable appearance data or cached resources with clear ownership. GameRuntime remains the owner of simulation state; AppKit drawing stays on the main actor. No simulation mutation from rendering.
integration.performance: Cache terrain/texture by stable identity; animate the lightweight view, not expensive noise generation every frame. Honour pause/reduced animation settings when supported. No render-time network/file I/O.

acceptance: Screen 6 visibly shows a shaded planet while docked and in space.
Selecting another planet or galaxy updates globe and facts together; returning preserves its terrain.
Lave and several other systems are visibly distinct; same name in another galaxy has its own stable identity.
Compact fonts stay the same logical size in small windows and full screen.
Facts, mission clues, PLUGH notes, messages, footer and cockpit HUD never overlap the globe.
Verify identity/seed determinism and rendering does not change simulation RNG/state with focused tests.
Inspect actual game-rendered screenshots at narrow and wide/full-screen sizes, then run make ci for the implementation. If README media changes, generate it only with make readme-media.
status: Research/design handoff; runtime implementation delegated to Elite Coder.
